newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UNION PLANS NO STRIKE IN ROTTERDAM PORT DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: UNION PLANS NO STRIKE IN ROTTERDAM PORT DISPUTE.

text.p: The FNV transport union said on Monday it was not about to call a strike in the port of Rotterdam and remained in discussions with labour pool company SHB about its plans to cut staff.
"The union is still in negotiations with the employers. The next round is on Wednesday and there are several other dates. We are at early stage," said union negotiator Niek Stam.
The meetings were scheduled for another month, he added.
The dispute centres around plans by SHB's management to make 200 of its 975 employees redundant by the beginning of July and to put 330 workers on a three-day week.

Last week the dispute escalated as some 300 workers launched a wild-cat strike and workers at other companies took limited solidarity action, but the port itself and individual companies were largely unaffected.

Stam said the union preferred a negiotiated solution to the dispute, but said, if discussions broke down, one option would be strike action, possibly calling on other workers in the port of Rotterdam.
"We have had three big collective agreements from 1989 to now. This affects all the employees in the port," he added.
